title: Landscaping Business Software (2026): 6 Tools, Real Prices
description: Landscaping business software for crews: LMN from $297/mo, Service Autopilot, Jobber, Kickserv, Yardbook and quote-only Aspire on cost and job costing.
h1: Landscaping business software for crews and growing companies
body:
Landscaping companies that run crews need more than a mowing calendar: estimates built from labor hours and materials, multi-day install jobs, job costing to see which jobs made money, and enough user licenses for every crew lead. This guide compares six tools on exactly that, using only what each vendor publishes. Every price was checked on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-21 (LMN, Aspire, Service Autopilot, Jobber, Kickserv, Yardbook). Anything a vendor doesn't publish is marked unknown. If you mostly mow and fertilize with one or two people, start with lawn care business software instead.

{{table:lmn,aspire,service-autopilot,jobber,kickserv,yardbook}}

The six tools

  • LMN by Granum: budgeting and estimating for crews. Starter is from $297/mo billed monthly and includes 1 office/crew lead license plus 5 crew member licenses. Professional is from $648/mo with 3 office/crew lead and 15 crew member licenses, and adds real-time job costing. Enterprise starts at 100 users (contact sales). Extra licenses cost a fee that isn't published, and there's a one-time onboarding fee (amount not published). Budgeting, overhead recovery, estimating, scheduling, the LMN Crew app and invoicing are in every plan. Full breakdown: LMN pricing.
  • Aspire: quote-only, for $1M+ companies. Aspire doesn't publish prices. Its FAQ says pricing depends on company size, complexity and the solution you pick, billed as one monthly license fee with no limit on users. Its invoicing page lists three tiers by annual revenue: Growth ($1M-$3M), Corporate ($3M-$15M) and Enterprise (over $15M). Implementation, training and support are included in the monthly fee. Electronic payments, payroll and GPS fleet management are quoted separately. Listed features include estimating, job costing, purchasing, inventory, equipment management, site audits and an offline-capable mobile app. For smaller companies, Aspire points to its lighter product, Crew Control (pricing not reviewed here).
  • Service Autopilot: automations and route optimization. All published prices are annual subscription rates, plus a sign-up fee whose amount isn't published: Startup $49/mo (1 business user, 1 mobile license), Pro $199/mo (1 business, 2 mobile), Pro Plus $499/mo (1 business, 5 mobile) and Elite (2 business, 8 mobile; request pricing). Its plan cards list multi-day jobs, route optimization, job costing, chemical tracking and snow dispatch as Pro additions, and automation workflows at Pro Plus. (The comparison table on the same page also ticks route optimization, multi-day jobs and job costing for Startup, so confirm with sales if you want Startup.) QuickBooks Online sync is included on Elite and call-for-pricing on Pro and Pro Plus.
  • Jobber: per-user plans, job costing on Grow. Core $29/mo, Connect $99/mo and Grow $149/mo billed annually for 1 user. Each extra user is $29/mo, or you can pick bundles (Grow: 5 users $229, 10 users $299, 15 users $399/mo billed annually). Job costing is on Grow, and crew scheduling and unlimited job photos are on Plus (5 users $399/mo billed annually). Month-to-month prices are higher (Grow 1 user $199/mo). Every person who uses the account in the office or the field counts as a user.
  • Kickserv: many users for a flat price. Start includes 5 users for $60/mo billed annually ($75/mo monthly), Run 10 users for $119/mo ($149 monthly) and Scale 20 users for $199/mo ($249 monthly). No contract, and a 30-day free trial. Dispatch mapping and GPS check-ins are on Run and up. Route optimization isn't listed on its pricing page.
  • Yardbook: the low-cost option. Starter is free and includes scheduling, estimates, invoices and routing. Business is $34.99/mo and Enterprise $49.99/mo; Yardbook says those are annual-plan prices and month-to-month rates differ (not shown). User limits aren't published. QuickBooks sync is Enterprise-only. Yardbook doesn't list job costing or crew-level budgeting, so it fits small crews better than multi-crew install companies. See Yardbook vs Jobber.

Monthly cost for a 6-person and an 18-person company

List prices in USD per month before card fees, add-ons and onboarding or sign-up fees. We used LMN's own license bundles as the two sizes: 1 office person + 5 crew (6 users), and 3 office + 15 crew (18 users). Each tool is priced at its cheapest published option that covers that many people and includes job costing where the tool offers it.

On month-to-month billing, Jobber Grow works out to $328/mo for 6 users and $586/mo for 18 users, and Kickserv to $149/mo and $249/mo. Service Autopilot publishes only annual rates. The cheapest tools on this table don't list everything the expensive ones do: Kickserv doesn't list route optimization, and Yardbook doesn't list job costing. Compare those rows in the table above before you choose on price. For a wider cost breakdown, including solo plans, see lawn care software cost and the field service software pricing tracker.

What to check for a landscaping company

  • Estimating from labor and materials. LMN builds estimates from your budget and overhead recovery, with material and labor calculators. Aspire and Service Autopilot list estimating and job proposals. Jobber's quotes add optional line items and rich visuals on Grow.
  • Job costing. Listed on LMN Professional, Service Autopilot Pro and up, Jobber Grow and up, and Aspire. Not listed for Kickserv or Yardbook.
  • Who counts as a user. LMN sells office/crew lead and crew member licenses, Service Autopilot business users and mobile licenses, Jobber and Kickserv count everyone who logs in, and Aspire has unlimited users.
  • Accounting. LMN syncs with QuickBooks Online on Starter and adds QuickBooks Desktop on Professional. Kickserv includes QuickBooks Online on every plan (Desktop is $50/mo on Run and up). Jobber syncs QuickBooks Online from Connect. Aspire keeps invoices and receivables itself and sends deposits and purchase receipts to QuickBooks or Acumatica.
  • Snow in the off-season. Service Autopilot has snow dispatch from Pro, and Yardbook's free plan covers snow removal. See snow removal software.

None of these vendors publish card processing rates on their pricing pages except Kickserv (Tap to Pay 2.9% + 30¢, other online card payments 3.9% + 30¢) and Jobber (2.9% + 30¢ online). Ask for rates in writing, then run through the software buying checklist before you move your customer list.

faq: What is the best software for a landscaping business?

It depends on size. For crews that budget and estimate by labor hours, LMN starts at $297/mo with 6 licenses. Companies with $1M+ in revenue can get a quote from Aspire (unlimited users). Jobber Grow ($149/mo billed annually for 1 user) adds job costing, Kickserv includes 5-20 users from $60/mo billed annually, and Yardbook has a free Starter plan.
How much does landscaping software cost?

From the published prices checked 2026-11-21: Yardbook is free or $34.99-$49.99/mo, Kickserv $60-$199/mo billed annually, Jobber $29-$399/mo billed annually depending on plan and users, Service Autopilot $49-$499/mo on annual rates plus a sign-up fee, and LMN $297 or $648/mo plus an onboarding fee. Aspire is quote-only.

No. Aspire says pricing varies by company size, complexity and solution, billed as one monthly license fee with unlimited users. Its revenue tiers are Growth ($1M-$3M), Corporate ($3M-$15M) and Enterprise (over $15M). Payments, payroll and GPS fleet management are quoted separately.
Which landscaping software includes job costing?
LMN Professional (real-time job costing), Service Autopilot Pro and up, Jobber Grow and Plus, and Aspire list job costing. Kickserv and Yardbook don't list it on their pricing pages.
Is there free landscaping business software?

Yardbook's Starter plan is free and includes scheduling, estimates, invoices and routing, with a 1% Yardbook fee on online payments on free accounts (plus Stripe fees). See our free field service software guide for other $0 plans.
